title: Noise to data and back
sub: 26 points under a 1-D diffusion. The data has two clusters; the score is computed exactly.

frames.caption: Data: two clusters, at +1.5 and −1.5 (the density on the left). Each line will track one data point as the forward process adds noise. Time runs left to right.
Early on, β(t) is small: points jitter but stay near their cluster.
The signal is shrinking (each step multiplies x by √(1−β)) while noise is added. The clusters blur together.
By t = 0.5, only 28% of the original signal is left (√ᾱ ≈ 0.28). Blue and orange are thoroughly mixed.
At t = 1 every point is a draw from N(0, 1) (right). Which cluster a point came from is no longer recoverable from where it ended up. Destroying the data needed no learning at all.
Reverse: start from pure noise at t = 1 and run the reverse SDE towards t = 0. Each step follows the score, ∇ log p<sub>t</sub>(x), plus fresh noise. (Lines are coloured by where they will end up.)
While t is large, p<sub>t</sub> is nearly a single Gaussian and the score just pulls gently towards 0.
At t = 0.5, p<sub>t</sub> is still a single bump. The points have spread out, but there are no clusters to head for yet.

Around t ≈ 0.33 the density splits in two, and the score starts pushing each point towards one side. That is when each point commits to a cluster, then gets pulled firmly in, still jittering from the injected noise.
At t = 0: samples from the two-cluster distribution, made from noise using only the score. In a real model the exact score is replaced by a trained network ε<sub>θ</sub>.
The same starting noise, now run through the probability flow ODE: the same score, half the score weight, and no injected noise.
Paths are smooth curves, not jittery ones: the same starting point always gives the same result.
The paths fan out as t approaches 0.33, where the density splits, but they never cross: two paths of an ODE cannot meet.
Because the map from noise to data is deterministic and invertible, it can also be run forwards to encode a real data point into noise. That is what DDIM exploits.
Different paths from the SDE run, the same overall distribution at t = 0. Smooth paths also tolerate big steps, which is why DDIM samples well in about 50 steps.
